learning_outcomes.text: Students master the physical nature of fields and their interaction with matter, and the mathematical concepts suitable for their description.
Students can understand the derivation of Maxwell's equations from a few selected basic observations and use them as tools for modeling and simulating important phenomena.

syllabus_topics: Mathematical fundamentals (Vector analysis, structures in space and time)
Electrostatics (Coulomb's law, electric field, electric charge and dipole distributions, electric force and electric energy)
Magnetostatics (Biot-Savart law, magnetic field, magnetic dipole distributions, magnetic force and magnetic energy)
Solution methods for field equations (Graphical methods, analytical methods, numerical methods)
Electrodynamics (Continuity equation and displacement current, induction effect, full Maxwell's equations, electrodynamics in matter)

Regimes of electromagnetic problems, applications (Electro- and magnetostatics, flow fields, electrostatic approximation, semiconductor technology, magnetostatic approximation, skin effect, energy technology, components and Kirchhoff's networks, rapidly changing fields, electromagnetic waves, dipole radiators)
assessment_rules: Credits are awarded upon successful completion of the module exam.
